Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing below and adding technical constraints.

Short answers up front:
- APAC residency pin: yes — for Medifi we will set your account routing affinity to APAC regions for primary inference and storage. This is configurable per-account and will be documented in Exhibit B. Noted: this is an affinity, not absolute immutability; we provide guarantees around where primary processing occurs.
- Transient edge hops: we limit cross-region transient hops to specific operational categories (cache warm-up, KV sync for model state, short-lived burst replication). Each transient hop is bounded to a maximum of 72 hours under our standard temporary hop policy; we can tighten to 48 hours for customers with strict needs via DPA addendum.

What we will provide in writing (next steps):
- A short Ops runbook excerpt that lists allowed hop categories and controls (attached).
- Exhibit B draft with APAC affinity language and the 48h/72h transient hop options noted as selectable slots.
- Telemetry export showing region-of-processing tags for the next 30 days so you can verify routing behavior during onboarding.

Questions for you:
- Do you require a hard-coded 48h maximum in the DPA, or would a selectable option (48h or 72h) be acceptable so procurement can choose the level?
- Any restricted data classes that must never leave APAC (e.g., certain PHI subsets)? If so, we need those enumerated for policy enforcement.

I'll loop in Priyom for the instrumentation/telemetry specifics and Marcus for the ops runbook.

Best,

Asha — adding technical color from infra/ops.

Operational constraints and controls we use to bound transient hops:
- Category filtering: only requests flagged as performance bursts or cache warm-up will be eligible for cross-region edge hops. Customer-level flags are applied at the routing layer.
- Token-level tagging: all wire requests include a region tag and account id; any hop that crosses region sets a transient flag and TTL.
- TTL enforcement: default TTL for transient KV/replication entries is 24 hours; replication windows triggered by capacity spikes may extend that to a hard upper bound of 72 hours.
- Audit & alerting: any cross-region hop writes an audit entry to the control plane and generates an alert if it extends beyond the DPA-bound threshold.

We can commit to the following for Medifi:
- Default transient max = 48 hours (ops will enforce TTLs and automatic scrubbing at 48h for keys/replicas associated with your account).
- An emergency 72h extension can be invoked only with a documented incident and is subject to post-incident review; the DPA can include the extension process.

Attachments: edge-hop-ops-runbook.txt (plain text, 12KB) — runbook excerpt with the enforcement hooks.

If helpful, we can produce a small sample telemetry export for a 72-hour rolling window to demonstrate enforcement.

Marcus Lin
